deadlines.citation: 29 CFR 2560.503-1(h)(3)(i): at least 180 days following receipt of an adverse benefit determination; HealthCare.gov: file within 180 days (6 months)
29 CFR 2560.503-1(i)(2)(ii): pre-service appeal decided not later than 30 days after receipt (one level)
29 CFR 2560.503-1(i)(2)(ii): 15 days per level when the plan has two appeal levels
29 CFR 2560.503-1(i)(2)(iii)(A): post-service appeal decided not later than 60 days after receipt (one level)
29 CFR 2560.503-1(i)(2)(iii)(A): 30 days per level when the plan has two appeal levels
29 CFR 2560.503-1(i)(2)(i): urgent care appeals decided not later than 72 hours after receipt
HealthCare.gov: file external review within 4 months after the date you receive the final determination
HealthCare.gov: standard external review decided no later than 45 days after the request
HealthCare.gov: expedited external review no later than 72 hours

categories.label: Plan exclusion
categories.plain_english: Your plan does not cover weight-management drugs at all. Criteria do not matter; appeals rarely change a written exclusion.
keywords: weight loss drugs are not covered

categories.label: Renewal: starting records missing
categories.plain_english: The renewal failed because the plan could not see your starting point to measure progress. The baseline record usually exists; it was not sent.
keywords: weight at the time the medication was started
unable to verify a weight loss
categories.source_note: Pattern seen in Michigan administrative hearing decisions on Zepbound renewal denials (Dec 2025).

categories.label: Missing or incomplete paperwork
categories.plain_english: The plan says records were not provided. This is the most fixable kind of denial: your doctor usually already has them.

categories.label: Diagnosis code missing or mismatched
categories.plain_english: The request did not carry a diagnosis code the policy accepts. Your doctor's office can correct the code and resubmit.

categories.label: Must try other drugs first
categories.plain_english: The plan wants another drug tried first. An appeal can work if that drug was tried, or is unsuitable for documented reasons.

categories.label: Not on the plan's drug list
categories.plain_english: The drug is not on your plan's drug list. You can ask for a formulary exception, or the plan may cover a preferred alternative.

categories.label: Quantity or dose limit
categories.plain_english: The amount or strength requested is above the plan's limit. Often fixed by correcting the prescription quantity.

categories.label: Clinical criteria not met
categories.plain_english: The plan reviewed the records and says the criteria are not met. Winnable when the records show otherwise; harder when they do not.

categories.label: Other or unclear
categories.plain_english: We could not match the reason to a known pattern. Ask the plan for the specific criteria not met; they must tell you.

winnability_weights.source_note: Editorial ranking weights used only to order and threshold the 'worth appealing?' score. They are NOT success probabilities. Context: KFF found insurers upheld 66% of 2024 HealthCare.gov appeals overall, with no breakdown by reason.

worth_appealing_min_score_usd.source_note: Editorial threshold: annual money at stake x winnability weight must reach this to label an appeal 'worth it'.

checklist_items.label: Copy of the denial letter
checklist_items.detail: Include the page with the reference number and the stated reason.

checklist_items.label: Chart note with baseline height, weight and date
checklist_items.detail: From before your first GLP-1 fill. Most patient portals have it.

checklist_items.label: Current measurements documented by your doctor
checklist_items.detail: Recorded alongside the baseline so the plan can compare them.

checklist_items.label: Weight-management program records
checklist_items.detail: Visit dates, dietitian or program notes covering the period your plan requires.

checklist_items.label: Diagnosis code confirmation
checklist_items.detail: Your doctor confirms the codes on the PA form match what the policy accepts.

checklist_items.label: Your plan's PA criteria page
checklist_items.detail: DoseCost attaches the policy excerpt with its page reference.

checklist_items.label: Letter of medical necessity, signed by your doctor
checklist_items.detail: DoseCost drafts the structure; your doctor writes and signs every clinical statement.

checklist_items.label: Record of the step-therapy drug
checklist_items.detail: Pharmacy history or a chart note showing the trial, or why it is unsuitable.

checklist_items.label: Your plan's benefit booklet (SPD) exclusions page
checklist_items.detail: Confirms whether the exclusion is written into your plan.

checklist_items.label: Ask about a formulary or medical exception
checklist_items.detail: Plans may grant exceptions case by case; ask HR or the plan in writing.

checklist_items.label: Ask the plan for the specific criteria not met
checklist_items.detail: The plan's notice must state the specific reason and the plan provisions it relied on.

context_stats.statement: Fewer than 1% of denied in-network claims were appealed (HealthCare.gov insurers, 2024).
